steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Crime: an act that breaks the law and is punishable by the state. Deviance: behaviour that violates social norms. Not all deviance is crime (dyeing your hair an unusual colour is deviant but legal) and not all crime is deviant (speeding is illegal but widely accepted). The boundary between crime and deviance changes over time (homosexuality was a crime until 1967 in the UK). | Key Fact: Deviance is socially constructed: what counts as deviant varies across cultures and time periods. Example: drink-driving was once socially acceptable but is now both deviant and criminal; smoking in public places was normal but is now deviant and restricted.
